title: Sales/CS: Consolidate enterprise feature asks into hypothesis-backed scoping bundles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success submit a steady stream of high-touch enterprise feature requests (non-bug). Requests arrive as disparate asks that are hard to compare, prioritize, and scope for engineering and solutions teams. This slows handoffs, increases rework, and causes inconsistent signals for Dedicated/Private product decisions.

Goal: Create a repeatable process and artifact set to consolidate enterprise asks into small sets of hypothesis-backed scoping bundles. Each bundle should be scored by impact, implementation risk, recurrence, and required integrations, and produce a 1-page scoping brief that PMs can hand to ENG/Design for a rapid feasibility pass.

What success looks like: Within 2 sprints the CS/Sales intake flow produces clustered bundles (<=10 per month) with 1-page briefs and econ proxies. Engineering can make go/no-go spending decisions within a single review meeting. Sales/CS get faster expectations and better presales collateral for customer conversations.
acceptance_criteria: A clustering rubric is documented that weights: account tier, ARR impact, recurrence probability, engineering effort (T-shirt), data sensitivity, and required integrations.
An intake-to-bundle pipeline exists: raw tickets -> triage playbook -> candidate clusters -> hypothesis scoping brief (1 page) -> engineering feasibility review.
Templates: intake form, cluster summary, and 1-page scoping brief are published in Confluence with examples populated from 6 historical requests.
Scoring: each bundle has a numeric score and recommended funding tier (no-go / low-effort pilot / scoped project / sales-supported build).
Handoff: engineering and design acceptance criteria and rough estimates are captured in the brief and linked to a follow-up ENG ticket when approved.
SLO: 90% of enterprise asks grouped into bundles and given a scoping brief within 10 business days of first CS submission.
A dashboard metric (sheet or Looker) tracks time-to-brief, bundle score distribution, and downstream conversion to ENG work.
Stakeholder alignment: Sales leadership and CS PoCs sign off on the rubric and one pilot bundle before rollout.
Security: any bundle touching customer data or requiring VPC/on-prem is flagged for security review in the brief.
A retrospective at the end of the pilot documents trade-offs and adjustments to the rubric.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff with Sales ops and two CS leads (Acme & Nova). Collected 18 open asks from last quarter to use as seed data.

2026-03-03 — Victor Chang: Drafted clustering rubric. Proposal: weight ARR impact x2, recurrence x1.5, engineering effort inverse weight. Shared with ENG leads for feedback (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pm/pm-92547/rubric-draft).
2026-03-04 — Mari Lopez (Sales): Feedback — rubric needs explicit field for compliance/regulatory asks; suggested adding 'compliance delta' + mandatory security flag.

2026-03-05 — Product sync: agreed to pilot with 6 asks grouped into 2 bundles (billing integrations, role-based export). Created two sample 1-page briefs in the Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/pm-92547-pilot.
2026-03-07 — Engineering review (Victor): ENG estimated bundles as 'pilot' (2w spike) and 'scoped project' (8w). Linked follow-up ENG tickets: ENG-21344, ENG-21345.
2026-03-08 — Design review (Lina Park): requested acceptance-criteria detail for UX flows; added 'example prompts' section for any LLM behavior-dependent ask.
2026-03-09 — Aisha Patel: Updated templates and published final intake form. Next: run pilot with Sales/CS for 30 days and track metrics. Dashboard ticket created: PM-92547-DASHBOARD.
Notes: Keep bundle sizes small (3–6 requests max) to keep briefs actionable. Avoid over-aggregating unrelated asks under a single 'platform' label.
